payload.reasonForStatus: Test harness (scripts/verify-mudanca-negocio-slide-deck.cjs) is written, wired into agentic.config.yaml as a blocking gate check (e2e-mudanca-negocio-slide-deck), and confirmed deterministic (3/3 identical runs). It currently FAILs (56 of ~90 assertions) because frontend-dev's implementation did not exist on disk at authoring/run time — presentations/mudanca-para-negocio/index.html, css/, and js/ are unmodified from the pre-spec baseline (confirmed via git diff against origin/main). This is a genuine, honest FAIL of the gate against the sealed spec's acceptance criteria, not a defect in the test suite. Re-run this check once frontend-dev's implementation lands; do not weaken any assertion to make it pass.

coverageReport.justification: No coverage instrumentation exists in this repo, by design (CLAUDE.md: static, build-free, no package.json/lockfile/node_modules). Reporting a percentage would be fabricated. The QA substrate here is scripts/verify-mudanca-negocio-slide-deck.cjs, a real Playwright script driving actual Chromium against file:// URLs and asserting on DOM visibility, computed styles, URL/history state, and keyboard/touch/click interaction — same precedent as scripts/verify-hero-pan.cjs and scripts/verify-agentic-first-sdlc.cjs, neither of which report coverage percentages either.

mutationReport.note: Not measurable: no mutation tool exists or is introducible without a package.json this repo prohibits. No ComponentManifest/mutationScope tags were available for this spec (none existed at authoring time). Recorded as unavailable, not as a passing or failing score.

crapScore.note: CRAP = complexity x coverage requires a coverage axis that does not exist here. Structural complexity was kept low per-function (each check function is a flat, linear sequence of goto/assert steps; no function exceeds the repo's static-structure complexity budget of 15 - static-structure check passes clean).

AC6_manifest_driven_slide_order_not_hard.gap: This AC is fundamentally about internal code structure (a config array vs. hardcoded per-section navigation logic), which a black-box E2E script cannot directly inspect if the implementation keeps the manifest module-private (which is equally spec-compliant). Recorded as a best-effort probe plus a note, not a hard pass/fail — a code-review-level check (not available to this agent without reading frontend-dev's implementation, which the QA charter forbids doing to derive assertions) is the only way to fully close this gap. NOT silently dropped: emitted as a NOTE in the run log either way.

This is a reasonable, standard E2E approximation of a CSS-only-hiding requirement, not a compromise on the assertion itself (any non-hero visible at this point is still a real FAIL).

automated_tests: checkNoPageScroll: for both a 375x667 mobile viewport and a 1440x900 desktop viewport, for every one of the 5 slides via ?slide=N, assert document.documentElement.scrollHeight <= innerHeight+2 and scrollWidth <= innerWidth+2

AC10_100vh_100vw_no_page_scroll_no_clipp.gap: This checks 'no page-level scroll', which structurally implies 'each slide fits its viewport' but does not independently re-verify specific CTA/title elements are not clipped inside that box (a more granular per-element boundingRect-vs-viewport check was scoped out for time; the page-level scroll-absence check is the strongest single proxy available without a manifest naming which elements are 'essential').

automated_tests: checkVideoPauseOnNavigateAway: click [data-video-play], confirm it actually plays, ArrowLeft away, assert video.paused === true, and assert zero page errors were thrown throughout
AC12_video_pauses_on_navigate_away_silen.coverage: PARTIAL (best-effort, as explicitly invited by the task)
AC12_video_pauses_on_navigate_away_silen.gap: Video DID start playing (existing js/video.js behavior, PASS) but pause-on-navigate-away correctly FAILs today since there is no deck to navigate away with. Could not construct a reliable, non-implementation-reading way to simulate 'pause() throws before video.js is ready' (that requires either monkey-patching HTMLMediaElement.prototype.pause before the page's own script runs, or knowing the exact lifecycle hook the real implementation calls) — documented here as a best-effort limit rather than silently dropped. Recommend the build agent expose a small, deterministic hook (e.g. a custom 'hotsite:slidechange' event) so a future revision of this test can dispatch it directly with pause() overridden to throw, instead of racing real navigation.

Recommend revisiting once the real transition duration is implemented and can be awaited via a transitionend/animationend event rather than a wall-clock guess.

EC_pushstate_replacestate_failure_in_res.reason: This is an explicit deferred_decision in the sealed spec itself (owner: PO, expires 2026-10-03, not yet confirmed even at seal time). Reliably forcing history.pushState/replaceState to throw inside a real Chromium page (short of monkey-patching before the app's own script runs, which risks testing the monkey-patch rather than the app) was judged out of proportion to a still-deferred requirement. Recommend revisiting once the PO resolves the deferred decision and/or the implementation exposes a fallback path this test can target directly.

EC_print_shows_only_current_slide_defaul.reason: The sealed spec itself accepts default browser print behavior as the expected result (out of scope for a dedicated print layout) — there is no behavior here to assert against beyond 'the browser does what it always does,' which this suite does not touch or interfere with.

flakinessLog.note: 3/3 runs produced byte-identical output (diffed run-to-run) — deterministic, non-flaky failure due to missing implementation, not intermittent test instability. Not quarantined: a consistently-failing test pinned to a real gap is not a flaky test.

contractViolations: No ApiContract exists for this spec (there is no API — it's a purely client-side static deck), and no ComponentManifest/WireframeSpec artifact was produced or found in agent-handoffs/ at authoring time (needs_prototype: true was set, but no wireframe output existed). This QA harness therefore had to propose its own selector contract for the deck's chrome (next/prev buttons, dots, counter) from the spec's prose vocabulary and this repo's existing data-attribute convention, documented in scripts/verify-mudanca-negocio-slide-deck.cjs's file header. This is not a violation by frontend-dev (nothing was implemented yet to diverge), but it IS a process gap worth flagging: if frontend-dev's eventual implementation uses different selector names, every control-dependent assertion in this suite will report a named 'control located: FAIL' rather than a false pass or a silent skip - which is by design, but will require a coordination pass (either frontend-dev adopts this file's documented selector contract, or this file is updated to match a real, reviewed contract - never the reverse of silently relaxing an assertion to fit whatever selectors happen to exist).
